correctness.rationale: For the Euclidean root lattice A4 in the zero-sum five-space, the Voronoi cell is exactly the coordinate-range<=1 polytope by root inequalities and z_i^2>=|z_i| for integral zero-sum lattice points. Its vertices have k high coordinates and squared norm k(5-k)/5, so mu^2=6/5. For every directed Hamilton path root frame, each permutation simplex has a uniform binary-coordinate translation and a containing sphere of squared radius k(5-k)/5<=6/5. The published general mu<=kappa bound supplies equality. Conversely any optimal frame has every subset sum squared norm<=4 (integral even squared norm and diameter<=2 sqrt(6/5)); no coordinate row can repeat positive or negative incidence. A squared-norm-four vector forces either >10 entries or dependent columns, so all four are roots; indegree/outdegree<=1 and connected rank four yield exactly an oriented five-vertex Hamilton path, 5!=120 full lattice bases. Independent exact integer enumeration of 50 short vectors and 230300 four-subsets produced exactly these 120, and 2880 packet witness checks in original verifier were inspected. Enumeration corroborates the infinite geometric proof; not its substitute.
